rationale: This sample is the Shootout 'matrix' benchmark: a small, compute-dense numeric program whose entire runtime is spent in a few hot loops (matrix multiply/inner products), so control-flow-flattening-style transforms that insert dispatcher overhead (FLA, BCF) get high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so they are only applied when a function's features strongly justify it, protecting the hot loops from multiplicative slowdown. Cheap, loop-safe transformations are favored instead: SUB (instruction substitution) has low runtime and size impact and adds strong local diversity, and SPLIT and IGV are nearly free structural diversifiers, so their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights stay low to encourage their selection broadly. IBR and ICALL receive moderate weights: indirect branching/calls complicate static analysis of call/branch structure but add per-invocation indirection cost, so they are enabled selectively for the few larger functions rather than blanket-applied; ICALL also carries a slightly elevated CorrectnessRisk weight since indirect call lowering can interact with varargs/attributes. With no source-level feature profile available (empty static profile), the table biases toward transformations whose cost is proportional to code size rather than execution frequency, maximizing reverse-engineering resistance per unit of overhead while keeping correctness risk low across the board.
